title: Certificates of Deposit: Assembling the Rate and APY of a Renewed Term
content:
This page states, for Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit, how the interest rate and APY of a renewed term are put together from the tier's published figure and the bonuses the new term has earned, and when a renewal is written at all.

## How the figures combine

- **Interest rate of the new term:** start from the tier's published standard interest rate; if the new term earned the Jumbo Bonus, the tier's Jumbo Bonus points go on; if it earned the Relationship Bonus, the tier's Relationship Bonus points go on as well. Both sets of points sit directly on that one standard rate, side by side. Rounding, half-up to 2 decimal places, happens a single time, once every addition is made.
- **APY of the new term:** assembled the same way from the tier's published standard APY, with the identical bonus points.

A bonus not earned contributes nothing; there is no other bonus.

## When a renewal is written

A renewal is written only when all three hold: the renewal has become owed, the certificate's record instructs renewal, and the certificate continues in its own tier. If any of them fails, no renewal is written and no rate is set.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures, not any tier's published rates)

Take a tier that publishes 3.61 percent as its standard interest rate and 3.68 percent as its standard APY, with a Jumbo Bonus worth 0.12 points and a Relationship Bonus worth 0.18 points.

| Bonuses earned by the new term | New interest rate | New APY |
|---|---|---|
| Both | 3.61 plus 0.12 plus 0.18, that is 3.91 percent | 3.68 plus 0.12 plus 0.18, that is 3.98 percent |
| Jumbo Bonus only | 3.73 percent | 3.80 percent |
| Relationship Bonus only | 3.79 percent | 3.86 percent |
| Neither | 3.61 percent | 3.68 percent |

## Point of judgement

**The owner's old term carried a higher rate than the new published figure.** The new term's rate is built only from the figures described here; the old term's rate plays no part.
